newsitem.title: USA: Secure Computing sees $0.31-$0.36/shr Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Secure Computing sees $0.31-$0.36/shr Q4 loss.

text.p: Secure Computing Corp said Thursday it expects to report a fourth quarter loss of $0.31-$0.36 a share, below analysts' expectations.
According to First Call, the mean analyst estimate called for a loss of $0.13 a share in the quarter, compared to a $0.04 a share profit a year ago.
The company also said chairman Kermit Beseke resigned. Also resigning was Don Whitbeck, vice president of International Sales and Customer Service.

The resignations come as the company said it will have lower than expected revenues of $8.6 million to $9.1 million in the quarter, due to large pending sales that did not close in the quarter. The computer network security company reported $9.1 million in revenues in the year ago quarter.

"This is symptomatic of what the new management team needs to address, namely a need for much stronger marketing and sales so that Secure Computing can capitalize on its exceptional technologies in the growing network security market and be less dependent on large customers," chief executive Jeff Waxman said in a news release.
Waxman joined the company in November.
A new chairman is expected to be named following the January 24 board of directors meeting, Secure Computing said.
Secure Computing shares were unchanged at 8-1/8 Thursday.
